blocks.content: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 constitutionalized the three-tier Panchayati Raj system, empowering local self-governance across rural India.

rows: Direct implementation of local civic amenities and welfare programs
Coordination and aggregation of plans submitted by Gram Panchayats
District-wide development planning, supervision, and fund distribution

items: Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended the 3-tier Panchayati Raj system, whereas the Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) proposed a 2-tier system.
Rajasthan was the first state to establish Panchayati Raj, inaugurated in Nagaur district on October 2, 1959.
Article 243I mandates the creation of a State Finance Commission every 5 years, and Article 243K establishes a State Election Commission.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 added Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O) and the 11th Schedule to the Constitution of India.
The Panchayati Raj system establishes a uniform three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat (village level), Panchayat Samiti (block level), and Zilla Parishad (district level).
States with a population under 20 lakhs are exempted from constituting the intermediate (block) tier.
A minimum of one-third (33%) of all seats and chairperson positions are reserved for women across all three tiers.
The tenure for every Panchayati Raj Institution is fixed at 5 years, and fresh elections must be conducted within 6 months in case of dissolution.
